items.title: Ray Ricker interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 27, 2022
items.q: I was taking lessons from Leon Russianoff in New York

ctx.x: I gleaned a lot of wonderful information from your book which we’ll get to. I understand the Vietnam war played a role in your decision about what direction to go when you were I guess late teens, early twenties?

Yeah well actually I was a little older than that because I think that was — I went in the Army in 1967. And I was there for three years, ’67 to ’70. But yeah, I was going to get drafted. And I already had, well I was finishing up my master’s degree at Michigan State and was getting ready to get married too. But my deferment, the day I got my degree, right after that I think it was on the weekend, on that Monday or Tuesday I got the “Welcome to the Army” draft notice. I went from 2S which was student, to 1A which…
I understand that you and some of your mates grew mustaches as a mild form of protest?
